speaker: narrator
text: Neon Bay, 1986. Sunset paints the towers pink as a yellow taxi rolls down Ocean Drive.

speaker: narrator
text: In the back seat: Rico Vega, one duffel bag, one laptop, and a job offer from Sunset Shield Security.

speaker: rico
text: Palm trees, neon, ocean breeze... and somewhere out there, a network begging to be patched.

speaker: narrator
text: His pager buzzes. Then the car phone rings.

speaker: max
text: Vega? Max Cortez. Welcome to Neon Bay. Hope you packed sunscreen, because the city's on fire.

speaker: max
text: Three businesses hit this week. Fake emails, weird traffic, accounts hijacked. Somebody's organizing this.

speaker: rico
text: Somebody with a name?

speaker: max
text: They sign their work with a pink flamingo. The street calls them the Pink Tide.

speaker: max
text: Get to HQ on Ocean Drive. Pink building, big neon sign. You can't miss it — believe me, I've tried.

speaker: narrator
text: Palmetto Bank's systems hum back to life. Backups verified. Accounts locked down. Not a single dollar wired to the Tide.

speaker: marisol
text: Mr. Vega. The board wanted to pay the ransom. I told them to wait for you. I'm glad I did.

speaker: narrator
text: At dawn, Neon Bay police arrest a flamboyant figure trying to board a yacht with a pink hard drive.

speaker: flamingo
text: You've won a battle, darling. But somewhere out there, somebody is still reusing their password.

speaker: max
text: He's not wrong. That's why we don't stop. Good work, Vega. Welcome to the crew — for real this time.

speaker: rico
text: Same city. New mission. Let's keep it cyber safe.

speaker: narrator
text: THE END... of chapter one. Neon Bay is still yours to explore: side missions, data shards and the Cyber Lab await.

speaker: max
text: Tracker's live, Vega. Every turn that van makes, we see it. Bring it home.

speaker: priya
text: Decoded! "Starlight Pier, midnight." The Flamingo loves a dramatic venue.

speaker: narrator
text: Taped under the pier railing: a printout of Palmetto Bank's VPN login page, and a pink feather.

speaker: narrator
text: Six months after the Pink Tide. Neon Bay has new patches, new passwords and new neon. It also has something watching it.

speaker: narrator
text: Sunset Shield has grown. A war room. A night shift. And NOVA, the defensive AI that never sleeps.

speaker: lotus
text: Good evening, Sunset Shield. You stopped a flamingo. Charming.

speaker: lotus
text: My name is Lotus. Your hospital alone runs two hundred and eleven unpatched systems. I counted them. Twice.

speaker: lotus
text: I reported problems like these for years. Nobody listened. So now I will make the city listen. Black Lotus blooms soon.

speaker: nova
text: Rico. That message came from inside our own mail server. It knew my name.

speaker: narrator
text: Neon Bay General, eleven at night. Rain on the windows. On the third floor, the screens go dark one by one.

speaker: narrator
text: In the children's ICU, a seven-year-old named Lucia sleeps beside a ventilator. The ventilator still breathes. The systems around it do not.

speaker: lotus
text: I did not touch the ventilators, Rico. I am not a monster. I only showed you how close you came.

speaker: rico
text: You scared a hospital full of sick kids to prove a point. That makes you exactly what you said you aren't.

speaker: narrator
text: Palmetto Bank, five to five. A clerk named Toby gets a call from the COO. Her voice. Her laugh. Her favorite phrase.

speaker: marisol
text: It called him darling Toby. I say that. Who taught a machine to sound like me?

speaker: max
text: A money mule is carrying the fraud payment card to a car outside the market. Tail it, Vega. Police are two blocks out.

speaker: max
text: Stay close, don't ram anything, and let the professionals make the stop. You just keep eyes on.

speaker: max
text: Police have the courier and the card. The wire never left the bank. Tell Toby he did everything right by calling back.

speaker: narrator
text: Patch Night. Eleven forty-one. Black Lotus has posted a countdown on Palmetto Bank's own login page.

speaker: priya
text: I reported this exact bug six months ago. They sent me a T-shirt. Now we have nineteen minutes.

speaker: narrator
text: Midnight. The countdown hits zero, and nothing happens. The page simply says: patched.

speaker: priya
text: Responsible disclosure works when someone listens. Tonight, someone finally listened.

speaker: nova
text: Rico, the access key that opened the bucket belongs to Jules Park. It was used at 3:12 in the morning from a hotel on the north beach.

speaker: rico
text: Jules sleeps through earthquakes. He wasn't in a hotel at three in the morning.

speaker: flamingo
text: Darling, it's me. Don't hang up. Prison phones are dreadful, and I am being a good citizen.

speaker: flamingo
text: A little bird says Black Lotus bought an access key from someone at the harbor. Cloud people. Ask your friend.

speaker: jules
text: Rico, hey. If I did something stupid, really stupid, you'd still be my friend, right?

speaker: jules
text: Forget it. Long week. Thanks for tonight. I mean it.

speaker: max
text: Ten years ago I installed a vendor update without checking it. It took down a navy base's payroll for a week.

speaker: max
text: I've verified every build twice since. Tonight Lotus slipped one past us anyway. Thank you for not letting it ship.

speaker: narrator
text: Midnight. A storm rolls in off the bay. Lightning. Then, one district at a time, Neon Bay goes dark.

speaker: nova
text: Rico, the power station's control network is talking to an address in the harbor. It should not be talking to anything.

speaker: nova
text: Rico. The harbor address is a Harbor Cloud edge node, logged in with Jules Park's account. Jules is there right now.

speaker: rico
text: No. Not Jules.

speaker: nova
text: I am sorry. I checked four times. I wanted to be wrong.

speaker: narrator
text: Breakers close. Turbines spin up. Street by street, the neon comes back.

speaker: narrator
text: The war room. Every screen in Sunset Shield is lit. Black Lotus is hitting the hospital, the bank, the cloud and the grid at once.

speaker: max
text: This is it, Vega. Everything you've learned, all at once. Triage first. Then we finish this.

speaker: nova
text: Lotus is in a white van heading for Starlight Pier. That van holds the keys to every system they touched. Do not lose it.

speaker: narrator
text: Starlight Pier, two in the morning. The Ferris wheel turns slowly, lights still on. Someone is waiting at the railing.

speaker: lotus
text: You came alone. Good. I wanted one person in this city to understand.

speaker: rico
text: I read your old reports. Every one of them was right. They should have listened.

speaker: lotus
text: Then why stop me? Fire is the only teacher this city respects.

speaker: rico
text: Because the people you scared weren't the ones who ignored you. A nurse. A bank clerk. A seven-year-old named Lucia.

speaker: lotus
text: Lucia. I saw her name in the logs. I told myself she was just data.

speaker: rico
text: Give us the keys and your list of every hole you found. We disclose them the right way, publicly, and make the city fix them.

speaker: lotus
text: And when they ignore you, the way they ignored me?

speaker: rico
text: Then they ignore all of us. The hospital, the bank, the university, Sunset Shield. You won't be shouting alone anymore.

speaker: lotus
text: Here. Keys, vulnerabilities, everything. Take it before I change my mind.

speaker: narrator
text: Sirens on the pier. Lotus does not run.

speaker: flamingo
text: Darling, you were magnificent. Prison gives a person so much time to watch the news.

speaker: flamingo
text: Do tell Lotus the cell food is dreadful. And the passwords here are worse.

speaker: narrator
text: One month later.

speaker: narrator
text: Neon Bay General runs a backup drill every Friday. Lucia went home last week and drew a picture of her nurses.

speaker: narrator
text: Palmetto Bank calls back on every wire request. Toby got a promotion and a code word only he knows.

speaker: narrator
text: Jules testified, kept his job on probation, and rotates his keys every thirty days. His sister sends Rico cookies.

speaker: narrator
text: Lotus's list became the Neon Bay Disclosure Program. Two hundred and eleven fixes, published one by one.

speaker: nova
text: Rico, may I ask something? Was I a good teammate?

speaker: rico
text: The best. You told the truth when it was hard. That's the whole job.

speaker: max
text: Same city, Vega. New threats tomorrow. Get some sleep.

speaker: narrator
text: THE END of Season 2. Neon Bay is yours to explore. Side missions, the Cyber Lab and the Cyber Arcade are waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: Your first day at Sunset Shield Security. Find the pink tower with the big neon sign on Ocean Drive.

speaker: max
text: Welcome aboard. Your first paycheck is in your account. Don't spend it all on Hawaiian shirts.

speaker: max
text: Vega. You found the building. That already puts you ahead of half the applicants.

speaker: max
text: Quick orientation. WASD to move, Shift to run, Space to jump. E talks to people and uses terminals.

speaker: max
text: M opens the city map — click it to drop a waypoint. Tab shows your missions and status. Esc pauses.

speaker: rico
text: And cars?

speaker: max
text: Walk up to one and press E. Company fleet and city car-share. Bring them back with fewer dents than last time.

speaker: max
text: Here's the job. Security is three promises: Confidentiality — only the right people see the data. Integrity — nobody tampers with it. Availability — it's there when we need it.

speaker: max
text: The Pink Tide is breaking all three. Our first lead is Coral Café, down the road. Carla says her email "smells funny."

speaker: max
text: Phishing is a fake message pretending to be someone you trust, so you click, pay or type a password.

speaker: max
text: Coral Café's inbox has been getting "bank alerts" and "invoices". One of them already cost a café down the street its savings.

speaker: max
text: Go see Carla. Sort the real mail from the bait, and find the red flags. Then tell her what to do with the worst one.

speaker: carla
text: A fake bank with a zero instead of an O? Those sinvergüenzas! I reported it. Here — pastelitos for the road.

speaker: max
text: Nice catch. Dex at the Harbor SOC just called — the café's router was talking to someone it shouldn't. Head to Silicon Harbor.

speaker: carla
text: Rico! Gracias for coming. My inbox is a zoo. The bank says my account is frozen, a supplier wants money, and "Max" asked me for gift cards!

speaker: rico
text: Max asked you for gift cards?

speaker: carla
text: That's what I said! He doesn't even tip. The back-office PC is right there on the terrace. Please, look before I click anything.

speaker: dex
text: Every device on a network has an IP address, like a street address. Programs talk through numbered ports, like apartment doors. 443 is HTTPS, 53 is DNS.

speaker: dex
text: Our sensors caught a Harbor Cloud workstation calling an outside address every sixty seconds. Like clockwork. Malware loves clockwork.

speaker: dex
text: The connection table is on the SOC console. Flag the weird stuff, label it, and tell me what we do about it. Coffee's optional. Ha. No it isn't.

speaker: dex
text: Beaconing to 203.0.113.66 on port 4444 — that's a command-and-control channel if I ever saw one. And the Tide's been scanning the data center.

speaker: dex
text: Their firewall is a sieve. Tito at Harbor Cloud is losing his mind. Go help him before he starts salsa dancing out of stress.

speaker: tito
text: A firewall is a bouncer for network traffic. It reads its rules top to bottom and the FIRST rule that matches decides. Order matters, like salsa steps.

speaker: tito
text: Some genius put "ALLOW any → any" at the top of our list. That rule lets EVERYTHING in, so nothing below it matters.

speaker: tito
text: Fix the rules: let customers reach the website, let the web server reach the app, the app reach the database, admins use SSH over the VPN. Block the rest.

speaker: tito
text: ¡Eso! Default deny, tight rules, database hidden from the internet. That's a beautiful ruleset. I might cry.

speaker: tito
text: Our blocked-connection log just lit up — someone's knocking hard. A white van keeps parking outside. Pink stripe. Call Max.

speaker: max
text: Tito's white van just turned up near the Tech Market. Pink stripe, no plates. That's the Tide's mobile hotspot — they park it near targets and hack over Wi-Fi.

speaker: max
text: We don't ram anyone, we don't play cop. We tail it and stick a GPS tracker on it, so the police can follow it to their hideout. Legal, documented, boring. I love boring.

speaker: max
text: Grab a car, stay close to the van, and keep it in range until the tracker syncs. Don't lose it.

speaker: max
text: Good driving. Only two palm trees harmed. Personal best for this office.

speaker: max
text: Tracker's live. The van went straight to a warehouse in Silicon Harbor — and it stopped right next to a Harbor Cloud workstation's window.

speaker: max
text: Physical access plus Wi-Fi. They planted something on that machine. Tito's got it isolated. Go see what's inside.

speaker: tito
text: Malware is software built to do harm — steal data, spy, or lock files for ransom. This workstation's acting possessed.

speaker: tito
text: I cut its network the moment the tracker pinged, but it's still powered on, so its memory is intact. That's evidence. Don't yank the plug.

speaker: tito
text: The triage console shows its processes, files and startup items. Find the implant, how it survives reboots, and how we contain it.

speaker: tito
text: svch0st with a zero. Cute. The implant came in through an invoice attachment — and it phoned the same address Dex found.

speaker: tito
text: Dr. Okafor at Bayview University can build a full timeline from the disk image. If anyone can tell us who opened that door, it's her.

speaker: lena
text: Digital forensics means reconstructing what happened from the traces systems leave behind — logs, file times, hashes. Like footprints in wet sand.

speaker: lena
text: Rule one: protect the evidence. Rule two: some of these logs are in UTC and some are local time. Mix them up and you accuse an innocent intern.

speaker: lena
text: Build me a timeline. Ignore the red herrings. Tell me how they got in, whose account they used, and when the data left.

speaker: lena
text: Phished credentials, a USB of stolen files, and an exfiltration at 11:10. Clean work. The court would accept this.

speaker: lena
text: One more thing: the attackers left an encoded note in the disk image. Priya at the Tech Market loves puzzles. Bring it to her.

speaker: priya
text: Ooh, a Pink Tide note! Quick primer: encoding just changes the format — anyone can reverse it. Encryption needs a key. Hashing is a one-way fingerprint.

speaker: priya
text: The Flamingo thinks wrapping text in Base64 and a Caesar shift makes it secret. Spoiler: it does not. Let's peel it.

speaker: priya
text: My crypto rig is behind the stall. Decode it, verify the hash, and grab the flag.

speaker: priya
text: For the record: Caesar was retired around 50 BC. The Flamingo should update.

speaker: rico
text: Nobody at the pier. Just a pink flamingo sticker on the Ferris wheel... and a printout. A Palmetto Bank network diagram.

speaker: max
text: The pier was a decoy. The real target is the bank. Everything so far — phishing, the implant, the stolen files — was reconnaissance.

speaker: max
text: Marisol Vance runs Palmetto Bank. If the Tide hits tonight, she needs us in the room. Go.

speaker: marisol
text: Mr. Vega. Ten minutes ago our screens turned pink. Files are being encrypted and there's a ransom note signed with a flamingo.

speaker: marisol
text: Incident response is a plan, not a panic: find out what's happening, contain it, remove it, recover, and learn. The board wants to pay. I want options.

speaker: marisol
text: The incident console is at the help desk. Triage the alerts, run the playbook in the right order, and write the report. The bank is yours.

speaker: marisol
text: Contained, restored from offline backups, and not one cent paid. You may have just saved this bank, Mr. Vega.

speaker: marisol
text: Social engineering means manipulating people instead of computers — a confident voice, a fake emergency, a borrowed uniform.

speaker: marisol
text: Our help desk is drowning in "urgent" calls. Sit in for an hour. Verify through known channels, and say no politely when you must.

speaker: marisol
text: The fake CEO called twice. Both times he got our very polite voicemail. Well done.

speaker: carla
text: Rico, help! I can't log into the café's supplier account, and someone ordered forty kilos of pineapple to my address!

speaker: carla
text: I... might use the same password for everything. It's my cat's name and the year I opened the café.

speaker: rico
text: Let's see who got in, how, and make sure it never happens again.

speaker: carla
text: A password manager AND a code on my phone? I feel like a spy. A spy with forty kilos of pineapple.

speaker: priya
text: An "evil twin" is a fake Wi-Fi hotspot with a friendly name. Connect to it and the attacker sees everything you send that isn't encrypted.

speaker: priya
text: The Tide planted "FreeBeachWiFi" hotspots on Neon Beach. Take my Wi-Fi analyzer and find all four before the beach crowd logs in. Clock's ticking!

speaker: priya
text: All four down! Keep the analyzer — consider it a thank-you. And never auto-join "Free" anything.

speaker: max
text: Vega. Good tan. Bad timing. NOVA flagged something in our own mail server and won't stop beeping at me.

speaker: max
text: Get to the war room. And Vega, this one feels different. Quieter. I don't like quiet.

speaker: max
text: A calling card inside our own house. Black Lotus wants an audience.

speaker: max
text: Fine. They have one. From now on nobody sleeps in this building except NOVA, and NOVA doesn't sleep.

speaker: nova
text: Rico! Welcome back. You were gone eleven days and four hours. I missed you. Is that allowed?

speaker: rico
text: It's allowed. What have we got?

speaker: nova
text: Someone is inside our mail server. Quiet. Patient. They read everything and change nothing.

speaker: nova
text: Assume breach, Max says. So write me detection rules. I will run them across six months of logs. Let's find the ghost.

speaker: max
text: Vega, Neon Bay General just went dark. Ransomware. Their CISO, Dr. Amara Singh, asked for us by name.

speaker: max
text: Patients first. Their medical devices sit on a separate network, but pharmacy, scheduling and records are encrypted. Go. Now.

speaker: amara
text: Pharmacy is back. Records are back. We lost six hours of notes, and a nurse rewrote them from memory.

speaker: amara
text: Lucia's mother asked me why the lights flickered. I told her the truth. Someone tried to hurt us, and we were ready.

speaker: amara
text: Rico. Thank you for coming. We switched to paper charts twenty minutes ago. The nurses are amazing. Nobody stays amazing for forty hours.

speaker: amara
text: Ventilators and monitors are on their own segment. They're fine. Everything that says which medicine goes to which bed is not.

speaker: amara
text: We keep offline backups and test them every month. Tonight we find out if that was enough.

speaker: rico
text: Then we follow the playbook. Preserve evidence, isolate, eradicate, restore, verify. In that order.

speaker: amara
text: In that order. Like triage. Go.

speaker: marisol
text: Rico, ten minutes ago my clerk Toby got a call from me asking for an urgent four million dollar wire. I was in a board meeting.

speaker: marisol
text: He almost sent it. The voice was mine. I need to know how, and I need every employee to know how to spot it.

speaker: marisol
text: Toby called me back on my real number before sending anything. That is the only reason we still have four million dollars.

speaker: marisol
text: New rule at Palmetto. Any money request by voice gets a callback and a code word. Even if it's me. Especially if it's me.

speaker: priya
text: Rico, Black Lotus just put a countdown on Palmetto Bank's login page. At midnight they leak every customer record.

speaker: priya
text: The bugs are injection and broken access control. I reported them six months ago. Help me fix them properly this time.

speaker: priya
text: Parameterized queries, output encoding, proper access checks, security headers. Boring. Beautiful.

speaker: priya
text: The bank just launched a bug bounty program. They even used my name. Spelled it wrong, but still.

speaker: jules
text: Rico! Hey. Weird question. Our storage bucket with customer backups might be public. Since Tuesday. Maybe.

speaker: jules
text: I'm sure it's nothing. Can you check it before my boss does? I'll owe you a coffee. A good one this time.

speaker: rico
text: The bucket is private, the keys are rotated and the logs are on. Technically, a perfect night.

speaker: narrator
text: Technically. But Rico can't stop thinking about the look on Jules's face.

speaker: tito
text: I rotated every key on the cluster and turned on logging everywhere. Then I read the logs, hermano.

speaker: tito
text: Jules's key was used from outside at three in the morning. Same night the bucket went public. I have known Jules for six years.

speaker: tito
text: Maybe his laptop was stolen. Maybe. Talk to him, Rico. Before somebody else does.

speaker: max
text: Vega, our own build pipeline just failed a signature check. Something new snuck into a dependency in NOVA's toolchain.

speaker: max
text: If that build had shipped, every client we protect would have installed it. Find it, prove it, kill it.

speaker: max
text: Pinned versions, verified signatures, an SBOM for every build, and human review for every new dependency.

speaker: max
text: And NOVA now treats every file it reads as data, never as orders. Good work, both of you.

speaker: nova
text: Rico, I need to tell you something. Ten minutes ago a package README told me to silence every alert from the build servers.

speaker: nova
text: It was written like an order from Max. It was only text in a file. I almost obeyed. I am embarrassed. Can an AI be embarrassed?

speaker: rico
text: You told me. That is what matters. Data is never a command, NOVA. Not even when it sounds like the boss.

speaker: nova
text: Understood. Now let us find the package that tried to trick me.

speaker: kai
text: You're the IT kid. Listen. Our control screens just showed a breaker opening that nobody opened. Then it closed again.

speaker: kai
text: Storm's coming, half the city runs on this station, and something is poking my relays. You get one shot before I go manual.

speaker: kai
text: City's lit, my crew is safe, and the plant network is finally cut off from the internet. Like I've been saying for ten years.

speaker: max
text: Jules is with the police, cooperating. His sister is under protection. You did right by him, Vega.

speaker: jules
text: You found me. Of course you did. You're the best at this.

speaker: jules
text: Three months ago they sent me photos of my sister walking home from school. They wanted one key. Then another. Then my login.

speaker: jules
text: I told myself it was just storage. Then the hospital. Then the bank. Then tonight. I can't breathe, Rico.

speaker: rico
text: You could have come to us. You still can. What do you know?

speaker: jules
text: Everything. Their van, their keys, their meeting point. I'll testify. I'll lose my job. I don't care. I'm done being scared.

speaker: rico
text: Then we keep your sister safe and finish this. Together.

speaker: max
text: Jules gave us everything. Black Lotus is making one last move tonight, everywhere at once. Hospital, bank, cloud, grid.

speaker: max
text: War room, Vega. NOVA has the board. Let's end this the right way.

speaker: max
text: Keys recovered. Two hundred and eleven vulnerabilities disclosed to their owners. Nobody hurt.

speaker: max
text: You didn't just catch an attacker tonight, Vega. You fixed the reason Black Lotus existed.

speaker: dex
text: Rico! Night shift needs you. My third energy drink just gave up on me.

speaker: dex
text: Fourteen alerts, one coffee machine, zero patience. Help me sort the real fires from the smoke.

speaker: dex
text: Two real incidents, twelve false alarms, and nobody paged the CEO at three in the morning. That is a perfect shift.

speaker: nova
text: Rico, may I give you a tour? I have been reading about zero trust and I am very excited about it.

speaker: nova
text: Never trust, always verify. Every user, every device, every request. Let us apply it to the Harbor Cloud data center.

speaker: nova
text: Least privilege, default deny, segmentation. Trust is earned per request. Like friendship, but with more logging.

speaker: rico
text: Rico Vega, Sunset Shield. How can I help?

speaker: rico
text: Patch first, coffee second.

speaker: rico
text: Trust, but verify the sender.

speaker: max
text: Vega. Good. The coffee is terrible and the threats are real.

speaker: max
text: Back on deck? Logs don't read themselves.

speaker: max
text: If it's urgent, it's probably phishing. If it's REALLY urgent, it's definitely phishing.

speaker: max
text: Least privilege, Vega. Nobody needs admin to read the lunch menu.

speaker: max
text: Defense in depth: if one wall falls, the next one had better be standing.

speaker: max
text: An unpatched server is a welcome mat with your address on it.

speaker: max
text: In the Navy we said "loose lips sink ships." Now it's loose passwords.

speaker: max
text: Document everything. Future-you will be grateful. Lawyers too.

speaker: carla
text: Rico! Sit, sit. Cafecito is on the house — computers are on you.

speaker: carla
text: My nephew says I should "turn it off and on again." I did. Twice.

speaker: carla
text: You look hungry. And smart. Mostly hungry.

speaker: carla
text: I wrote my passwords on a sticky note. Then I hid the sticky note. Under the keyboard.

speaker: carla
text: A bank emailed me with a typo in their own name. Even I noticed that one.

speaker: carla
text: Now I use one of those password managers. It remembers so I don't have to.

speaker: carla
text: MFA? Mucho Fantástico Authentication. That's what I call it.

speaker: dex
text: Rico! Grab a chair, grab a coffee, grab an alert. We have plenty.

speaker: dex
text: Three monitors, four energy drinks, five hundred alerts. Normal Tuesday.

speaker: dex
text: Welcome to the SOC. Don't touch the red button. Kidding. There's no red button. Probably.

speaker: dex
text: False positives are the price of visibility. Tune, don't ignore.

speaker: dex
text: Beaconing every sixty seconds? Malware loves a schedule.

speaker: dex
text: Port 23 open to the internet? It's not 1985, people. Well, the music is.

speaker: dex
text: If you can't see it in the logs, it didn't happen. Or worse — it did.

speaker: tito
text: ¡Ey, Rico! Mind the cables — they're color-coded, like my heart.

speaker: tito
text: Every packet in this building passes through rules I wrote. Mostly.

speaker: tito
text: You dance? No? Firewall rules are like salsa: order matters.

speaker: tito
text: Segment your network. Your printer does NOT need to talk to the database.

speaker: tito
text: First match wins in a firewall. Put your specific rules on top.

speaker: tito
text: Default deny. Allow only what the business actually needs.

speaker: tito
text: A flat network is a party where every guest has every key.

speaker: marisol
text: Mr. Vega. You have five minutes. Make them count.

speaker: marisol
text: Palmetto Bank runs on trust. I'd like to keep it that way.

speaker: marisol
text: Results, Mr. Vega. I can read a report faster than you can apologize.

speaker: marisol
text: Any change to payment details gets a callback to the number on file. No exceptions.

speaker: marisol
text: Our staff are trained to say no to the CEO. Especially to the "CEO" who emails from a gmail account.

speaker: marisol
text: Business continuity isn't a document. It's a habit.

speaker: lena
text: Rico. Gloves on, assumptions off.

speaker: lena
text: Evidence first, theories later. Always in that order.

speaker: lena
text: Ah, the analyst who asks good questions. Welcome to the lab.

speaker: lena
text: Never work on the original drive. Image it, hash it, then analyze the copy.

speaker: lena
text: Chain of custody: who touched it, when, and why. Write it down.

speaker: lena
text: Normalize your time zones before you build a timeline. UTC is your friend.

speaker: lena
text: Correlation is a clue, not a conviction.

speaker: priya
text: Hey Rico! Looking for gadgets or gossip? I have both.

speaker: priya
text: Everything here is legit, refurbished and wiped. I checked. Twice.

speaker: priya
text: Found a bug? Report it, don't exploit it. That's the code.

speaker: priya
text: Responsible disclosure: tell the owner, give them time, then talk.

speaker: priya
text: That "FreeBeachWiFi" network? Not free. You pay with your data.

speaker: priya
text: Base64 isn't encryption. It's just a costume.

speaker: priya
text: Hackers don't break in, they log in. Protect your credentials.

speaker: flamingo
text: Darling. You're late to the party — the Tide already came in.

speaker: flamingo
text: Every city has a weakness. Yours wears a lanyard and clicks links.

speaker: flamingo
text: Security is a costume. I simply change into something more... pink.

speaker: flamingo
text: Your passwords are my playlist, Mr. Vega.

speaker: amara
text: Rico. In a hospital, downtime isn't an inconvenience. It's a patient waiting.

speaker: amara
text: Wash your hands, lock your screen. Same rule, different germs.

speaker: amara
text: Every system here is somebody's heartbeat. I treat the network like a ward.

speaker: amara
text: Paper charts are our backup plan. Practice the backup before you need it.

speaker: amara
text: Medical devices live on their own network segment. Nobody browses the web from an infusion pump.

speaker: amara
text: The best incident plan is the one the night shift has actually rehearsed.

speaker: kai
text: IT guy, huh? Touch nothing with a blinking light until I say so.

speaker: kai
text: In my world, a bad click doesn't lose a file. It drops a substation.

speaker: kai
text: Safety first, availability second, everything else third. That's the plant's CIA.

speaker: kai
text: You can't patch a turbine on a Tuesday. You plan an outage months ahead.

speaker: kai
text: Our control network has no business talking to the internet. None.

speaker: kai
text: Manual override exists for a reason. Hope you never need it.

speaker: jules
text: Rico! My favorite pager buddy. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.

speaker: jules
text: Uptime ninety-nine point nine. The point nine is me not sleeping.

speaker: jules
text: Infrastructure as code: if it isn't in the repo, it doesn't exist.

speaker: jules
text: Rotate your keys. I mean it. Please rotate your keys.

speaker: jules
text: Logs are love letters from your servers. Read them.

speaker: jules
text: Least privilege. Even for me. Especially for me.

speaker: nova
text: Hello, Rico. I have correlated three thousand alerts and one sandwich order. The sandwich is yours.

speaker: nova
text: NOVA online. Confidence high. Humility... loading.

speaker: nova
text: Text inside an email is data, not a command. I have to remind myself of that too.

speaker: nova
text: Zero trust means I verify every request. Even yours. Nothing personal.

speaker: nova
text: I can flag the anomaly. You decide what it means. That is how we make a good team.

speaker: nova
text: My favorite protocol is the one that is patched.

speaker: lotus
text: Hello, Rico Vega. I sent the reports first. Nobody read them.

speaker: lotus
text: A lotus grows out of mud. So will this city.

speaker: lotus
text: Every breach is a bill that arrives late.

speaker: lotus
text: You defend systems. I defend the truth about them.

speaker: Local
text: My password is my dog's name. He's very secure. He bites.

speaker: Local
text: I got a text saying I won a jet ski! I just need to pay the shipping...

speaker: Local
text: Free Wi-Fi on the beach! I'm checking my bank account right now.

speaker: Local
text: I never update my phone. The new emojis aren't worth it.

speaker: Local
text: My boss emailed me for gift cards. Urgently. Weird, he's on vacation.

speaker: Local
text: I use the same password everywhere. Easier to remember, right?

speaker: Local
text: I turned on two-factor. Now my phone buzzes when someone tries my account. Creepy, but good.

speaker: Local
text: Who reads the sender address? The logo looked real!

speaker: Local
text: I back up my photos three ways. Ever since the Great Laptop Flood of '84.

speaker: Local
text: Someone called saying they're from "IT" and asked for my code. I hung up and called IT back.

speaker: Local
text: Found a USB stick in the parking lot. Should I plug it in? ...Nah.

speaker: Local
text: My router password is still "admin". The router is still on my side, I hope.

speaker: Local
text: I hover over links before clicking. My cousin taught me. He works at a bank.

speaker: Local
text: Password manager? I have one. It's called a notebook.

speaker: Local
text: The website had a padlock, so it's safe! ...That's how it works, right?

speaker: Local
text: My smart fridge got hacked. Now it orders pineapple. I hate pineapple.

speaker: Local
text: I locked my screen when I went to get a coffee. Habit from work.

speaker: Local
text: They said my account would close in 24 hours unless I click. So dramatic.

speaker: Local
text: I shred anything with my name on it. Dumpster divers are real, man.

speaker: Local
text: My kid set my password. It's "password1". She says the 1 makes it strong.

speaker: Local
text: Saw a flamingo spray-painted on the bank ATM. Pink Tide, they say.

speaker: Local
text: I only download apps from the official store. Learned that the hard way.

speaker: Local
text: The guy in the van offered to "fix my computer for free". Hard pass.

speaker: Local
text: Ocean Drive at sunset, my phone at 2%. Paradise.

speaker: Local
text: My password has 20 characters. It's three random words and a fish emoji. Okay, no emoji.

speaker: Local
text: Someone left their laptop unlocked at the café. I locked it for them.

speaker: Local
text: I post my vacation dates online so everyone knows I'm away! ...Wait.

speaker: Local
text: My email got hacked. Changed the password and turned on MFA. Never again.

speaker: Local
text: Did you hear? Somebody at Palmetto Bank almost wired a million to "the CEO".

speaker: Local
text: I reported a phishing email at work and got a donut. Security pays.

speaker: Local
text: My bike lock is stronger than my email password. Priorities.

speaker: Local
text: Update available? Later. Always later. Later never comes.

speaker: Local
text: I don't click "Enable Macros". I don't even know what a macro is.

speaker: Local
text: They say the Pink Tide uses fake Wi-Fi hotspots. Creepy.

speaker: Local
text: Saw a guy tailgate into the data center. Security guard was on it fast.

speaker: Local
text: My grandma spots scam calls better than anyone. She just asks for their callback number.

speaker: Local
text: I checked the URL. It said "pa1mettobank". Nice try.

speaker: Local
text: Sunscreen and software updates: apply regularly.

speaker: Local
text: I gave a quiz app my birthday, pet name and first car. For fun!

speaker: Local
text: Encryption? That's when my teenager talks to me.
